subject: ALLOCATE statement
notes: Read the format at specs/ISO_COBOL.md 22600-22604 (no 'Figure notes' block accompanies this diagram, so the transcribed <pre> IS the authority): ALLOCATE { arithmetic-expression-1 CHARACTERS | data-name-1 } [ INITIALIZED ] [ RETURNING data-name-2 ], with ALLOCATE / CHARACTERS / INITIALIZED / RETURNING underlined and no optional noise words. Read grammar rule `allocateStatement`: two alternatives, `ALLOCATE arithmeticExpression CHARACTERS INITIALIZED? (RETURNING dataReference)?` and `ALLOCATE dataReference INITIALIZED? (RETURNING dataReference)?` — arm-for-arm identical to the diagram, both optional phrases optional in both arms, and no scope terminator / conditional phrase (matching Table 12's empty ALLOCATE row at specs/ISO_COBOL.md:20867). Alternative order is safe because alt 1 requires the CHARACTERS token, so a bare data-name falls to alt 2 under ALL(*) prediction. The binder's `PtrBinder.BindAllocate` reads `al.dataReference()` (DIRECT children only, so data-names inside arithmeticExpression are not in the list) and indexes drefs[0] for data-name-1 / drefs[^1] for RETURNING — correct for all four legs, and the RETURNING()-null guard precedes the index so the no-RETURNING form cannot index an empty list. All five surface legs have goldens: `ALLOCATE G INITIALIZED RETURNING P`, `ALLOCATE W INITIALIZED`, `ALLOCATE 6 CHARACTERS INITIALIZED RETURNING P2` (2002/allocate_initialized), `ALLOCATE B` and `ALLOCATE 5 CHARACTERS RETURNING P` (2002/pointer_alloc). Editions: ALLOCATE appears in neither the 2023 new-features list (specs/ISO_COBOL.md 1100-1130) nor Annex E, so there is no 2014->2023 delta; it cannot be COBOL-85 because SR1 requires the BASED clause and SR3 requires category data-pointer, neither of which the 1985 standard has. || UPHELD: I re-read specs/ISO_COBOL.md 22598-22604 myself — the <pre> reads exactly `ALLOCATE ┤ arithmetic-expression-1 CHARACTERS | data-name-1 ├ [ INITIALIZED ] [ RETURNING data-name-2 ]`, brackets with NO choice-indicator bars, so INITIALIZED-before-RETURNING is a fixed order and the grammar's `INITIALIZED? (RETURNING dataReference)?` tail matches it in both arms. I re-read `allocateStatement` at CobolParserCore.g4:1244-1247 and `PtrBinder.BindAllocate` at PtrBinder.cs:99-138: for form 1 with RETURNING drefs has ONE element and drefs[^1] is it; for form 2 without RETURNING drefs has ONE element and drefs[0] is it; for form 2 with RETURNING drefs is [based, returning] and both indexes are right — all four index legs re-derived, not taken on trust. I do NOT rest on the ALL(*) prediction argument: `ALLOCATE B.` and `ALLOCATE G INITIALIZED RETURNING P.` are ENABLED goldens with byte-compared .out, which is empirical proof alt 2 is reachable. Edition re-derived independently of the code catalog: ALLOCATE is absent from Annex E (§E.2/§E.3, specs/ISO_COBOL.md 42858-44000), and §13.18.x SR16 (specs/ISO_COBOL.md:15101 — 'The BASED clause may be specified only in data description entries in the linkage section, in the working-storage section, and in the local-storage section. The level number of such data description entries shall be 1 or 77') plus §13.18.60.4 GR23's data-pointer are both post-85 constructs, so 2002,2014,2023. Not downgraded: the format-surface row is about which token sequences the grammar admits, and the BASED-record storage-shape gap found on GR3/GR4/GR7 is a data-model gap, not a surface one.
